title: Derive the settled-evidence cut-points from the arm's own purpose (expected armings per horizon), not from a picked share
note: [!] ID CORRECTED 2026-09-22 by the manager: this row was filed as E42 from a branch cut before #12725 landed, and E42 was taken on main by an unrelated row (the accounts.yaml symbol list). Two rows sharing an id is the collision E13 built a check for one level up, and it would have merged as a silent clobber rather than a conflict. Renamed to E47; no content changed. SPLIT OUT OF E41 BY THE LANE, 2026-09-22, so the flag could land today. The operator REJECTED the two proposed cut-points, verbatim: "we need data-backed values, not arbitrary ones (otherwise what's the point of the arm in the first place?)". PR #12745 lands the flag WITHOUT them -- it emits `settled_*` only where the verdict is invariant across the still-open cut-point band -- and this row is the derivation that closes the gap. [!] THE SPECIFICATION IS THE OPERATOR'S OWN PARENTHESIS. An arm exists to modify exits on trades that REACH arm_r, so the quantity that matters is not a bare share but EXPECTED ARMINGS PER HORIZON at the leg's own trade rate. A 5% reach share is ~10 armings/year on a leg trading 200 times a year and ~0.3 on a leg trading 6 times a year; those are different facts and one share-threshold cannot separate them. That also makes the threshold PER LEG, which is why the current band has to be leg-independent and therefore weak. [!] PROPOSED DERIVATION, written out so this needs no re-deriving. (1) expected_armings(leg, horizon) = reach_share * trades_per_horizon(leg). (2) trades_per_horizon is MEASURABLE TODAY and needs no new instrument: every comms/strategy_evidence/runs/<run>/<leg>__bt.json carries `total_trades` with `data_start` and `data_end`, so trades/day falls straight out; the same files already back the k/n in config/lever_reachability.json. (3) settled_inert when the CI-HIGH share implies FEWER THAN ONE expected arming over the horizon -- i.e. even the optimistic end of the interval predicts the lever never fires in that window. settled_reachable when the CI-LOW implies at least N. (4) [!] THE HORIZON AND N ARE THE PART THAT IS STILL UNDERIVED, AND THEY MUST COME FROM SOMETHING REAL -- the demotion-review cadence, the corpus span, the e35 re-check interval -- with the file saying WHERE EACH CAME FROM. Do not substitute a round number; that is the exact failure this row exists to correct. If the corpus cannot support a derivation, SAY SO and say what would: an honest 'cannot be derived from what we have' beats a second invented pair, and the flag already degrades safely to `unsettled` in that case. [!] WHERE TO WRITE IT: config/lever_reachability.json::evidence_flag_policy, replacing `plausible_cut_band` (or narrowing it) and flipping `status` off UNDERIVED. The grading code is scripts/ops/lever_evidence_flag.py::grade, which already reads the policy from the registry and already stores, per basis, the exact cut-points its own verdict flips at (`settled_reachable_if_reach_cut_at_or_below_pct` / `settled_inert_if_inert_cut_above_pct`) -- those are the inputs a derived threshold gets compared against, so the arithmetic is already laid out. Keep the self-test's non-vacuity control and add one showing a leg's flag MOVING when only its trade rate changes, which is the property this row adds. [!] WHAT THE DERIVATION WILL LIKELY SHOW, recorded in advance so it is falsifiable rather than confirmed after the fact: on the current corpus only uso_trend_1h clears any reachable bar, and NOTHING reaches settled_inert, because the inert side needs a horizon long enough that <1 expected arming is a real statement and the live populations are n=1 to n=37. If the derivation produces a confident `settled_inert` on a single-digit n, that is a sign the horizon was chosen to produce it.
